h1: The 8 Best Docking Stations for MacBook Pro of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: MacBook Pro Docking Stations: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 docking stations for MacBook Pro, from CalDigit and Plugable Thunderbolt docks to Anker hubs, scored on ports and displays.
summary: The CalDigit TS4 is the dock to buy for most MacBook Pro owners: certified Thunderbolt 4, 18 ports and a Mac-first track record. The Plugable 16-in-1 Thunderbolt 4 is the pick if you need dual 4K monitors validated for newer chips. The UGREEN Revodok Max 208 gives genuine Thunderbolt 4 for far less. Pro and Max owners with several displays should look at the CalDigit TS5 Plus, and the Anker 8-in-1 is the cheap travel option.
intro: Most dock buying mistakes with a MacBook Pro come down to one thing: the chip in your laptop decides how many external displays it can drive, and no dock can change that. A base M-series chip supports a single extra display natively, while Pro and Max chips handle more. A dock listing that says dual 4K can mean real Thunderbolt output or a DisplayLink workaround, and the difference shows up as compression and driver problems.

We reviewed eight docks and hubs, from Thunderbolt 5 flagships to a plain USB-C hub, and ranked them by connection type, display support, charging power and port count. Rankings come from spec sheets and owner-reported behavior. Check your own Mac's display limit before you buy, because that is the ceiling on every dock here.

products.name: CalDigit TS4 18 Port Thunderbolt 4 Dock
products.verdict: Certified Thunderbolt 4 with 18 ports, from a Mac-first dock maker.
products.description:
The TS4 is a certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 18 ports, the highest count in this ranking. CalDigit built its name on Mac docks, and the listing leans on native Thunderbolt display output and high bandwidth for mixed peripherals.

It beats the Plugable 16-in-1 on port count and long-term brand track record, while the Plugable wins on its explicit dual 4K validation. Against the TS5 Plus, the TS4 gives up Thunderbolt 5 but costs far less, and few MacBooks can use that extra bandwidth.

Buy it if you want one dock to hold a desk full of devices for years. Caveat: it is a big, pricey box if you only need a few ports.
products.idealFor: Desks with many peripherals that want a dock for years.
products.skipIf: You only need a handful of ports.

products.name: Plugable 16-in-1 Thunderbolt 4 Dock
products.verdict: 16 ports, 100W charging and dual 4K validated for newer MacBook chips.
products.description:
Plugable's 16-in-1 is certified Thunderbolt 4, passes 100W of charging and lists dual 4K monitor support validated for M4 and M5 MacBook Air and Pro. It is driverless and uses native GPU output, so it avoids DisplayLink compression.

It lands just under the CalDigit TS4 because it has two fewer ports and a shorter Mac track record, but its explicit dual 4K validation is more specific. Compared with the UGREEN Max 208, you get more ports and a validated claim for a higher price.

Best for Pro owners who want a no-driver dual monitor desk. Caveat: older M1 to M3 base chips still cap at one external display.
products.idealFor: Dual 4K desks on newer MacBook Pro chips.
products.skipIf: You run an older base M-series chip.

products.name: UGREEN 8-in-1 Thunderbolt 4 Docking Station (Revodok Max 208)
products.verdict: Genuine 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 with three downstream ports, for far less.
products.description:
The Revodok Max 208 is genuine Thunderbolt 4 at 40Gbps, with three Thunderbolt 4 ports, 85W charging and dual 4K at 60Hz or a single 8K display. UGREEN lists compatibility with M1 through M4 Pro and Max chips.

It ranks third because 85W is a little light for a 16-inch MacBook Pro under heavy load, and eight ports is far fewer than the TS4 or Plugable. In exchange it is the cheapest certified-style Thunderbolt option in the guide.

Best for a single-desk setup that needs high bandwidth rather than many ports. Caveat: check the 85W against your laptop's charger.
products.idealFor: High-bandwidth setups that do not need many ports.
products.skipIf: You charge a 16 inch MacBook Pro under heavy loads.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock (TBT-UDM)
products.verdict: Certified Thunderbolt 4, 100W charging and a compact body.
products.description:
The TBT-UDM is certified Thunderbolt 4 with 100W charging, dual 4K HDMI or a single 6K display, six USB ports, an SD reader and Ethernet. It sets up without drivers.

It ranks fourth because the 16-in-1 from the same maker adds ports and validation, and the UGREEN Max 208 offers more Thunderbolt ports. It is the sensible middle step in Plugable's range.

Best for a tidy desk where a compact dock is the priority. Caveat: dual monitors are HDMI only, so check your displays' inputs.
products.idealFor: Compact desks with one or two HDMI monitors.

products.award: Best for Pro and Max Multi-Display
products.name: CalDigit TS5 Plus Thunderbolt 5 Dock
products.verdict: Thunderbolt 5 bandwidth for multi-4K and 8K, aimed at Pro and Max chips.
products.description:
The TS5 Plus is CalDigit's Thunderbolt 5 flagship, aimed at M3 and M4 Pro and Max MacBook Pro owners who run several displays. It lists a high port count and the bandwidth for multiple 4K or 8K screens.

It ranks fifth only because few buyers can use it: Thunderbolt 5 needs a laptop that supports it, and it costs the most here. The TS4 is the better buy unless you really run three displays.

Best for editors with Pro or Max chips and a multi-monitor desk. Caveat: a base chip cannot use its extra headroom.

keySpecs.label: Aimed at
keySpecs.value: M3 and M4 Pro and Max

products.idealFor: Editors with Pro or Max chips and three screens.
products.skipIf: You run a base chip or one monitor.

products.name: Anker Prime TB5 Docking Station 14-in-1
products.verdict: 14 ports and Thunderbolt 5 for newer multi-display Mac setups.
products.description:
Anker takes on CalDigit with Thunderbolt 5 and 14 ports, pitched at the newest M4 and M5 multi-display desks. The listing highlights certified Thunderbolt compatibility and high bandwidth headroom.

It ranks below the CalDigit TS5 Plus because CalDigit has the longer Mac heritage, but it costs less. Against the TS4, you pay more for a bandwidth boost most owners cannot use yet.

Pick it if you are already on a Thunderbolt 5 Mac and want a cheaper path than CalDigit. Caveat: standard Thunderbolt 4 laptops will not see the benefit.
products.idealFor: Thunderbolt 5 owners who want a cheaper dock.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station 14-Port
products.verdict: 14 ports and up to 160W output, but not Thunderbolt certified.
products.description:
The Anker Prime 14-Port gives you 14 ports, up to 160W of output, dual 4K display support and 10Gbps data. It is a USB-C dock, not a Thunderbolt one, and the listing says so plainly.

It ranks seventh because it leaves out Thunderbolt, which limits display bandwidth and external drive speed. Against the Anker 8-in-1 below it adds ports and power for a modest step up.

Best for a budget desk that needs many ports and strong charging. Caveat: it will not match Thunderbolt docks for fast external storage.
products.idealFor: Budget desks that need many ports and power.
products.skipIf: You edit video from external SSDs.

products.name: Anker Laptop Docking Station 8-in-1
products.verdict: Dual HDMI, Ethernet, SD and 85W passthrough, for the lowest price.
products.description:
The Anker 8-in-1 is a USB-C hub with two HDMI ports, Gigabit Ethernet, an SD slot and 85W passthrough charging. It is the cheapest and most compact option in the guide.

It ranks last because it is a hub and not a certified Thunderbolt dock, so expect no high-speed storage and, on base chips, a second display that may not work. Compared with the Anker Prime 14-Port, you save money but lose ports.

Best for a light travel or temporary desk. Caveat: check that your chip supports two external displays first.
cons: Dual display limits on base chips
products.skipIf: Your main desk needs fast storage.

whatMatters.factor: Your chip sets the display limit
whatMatters.detail: A base M-series chip supports one external display natively. Pro and Max chips handle more. A dock cannot raise that ceiling unless it uses DisplayLink, which compresses the picture. Find your Mac's limit in Apple's tech specs, and then choose a dock that fits within it.

Thunderbolt 4 offers 40Gbps and drives monitors and fast drives together. A plain USB-C hub tops out lower, often around 10Gbps. If you move large files or run two screens, pay for Thunderbolt. Look for the lightning bolt logo and certified in the listing.

whatMatters.factor: Charging wattage must cover the laptop
whatMatters.detail: A 14 inch MacBook Pro charges comfortably at around 70W, while 16 inch models can draw more under load. A dock at 85W or 100W is fine for most. If the dock's wattage falls short, the laptop may drain while you work.

List your devices first: monitors, drive, keyboard, webcam, Ethernet. Then compare against the dock's downstream ports. Extra Thunderbolt ports matter more than extra USB-A, because they can chain further docks or fast drives.

Most docks ship with a short Thunderbolt cable, around 0.8 meters. If your desk layout needs more, a longer certified Thunderbolt cable costs extra. Check the cable length in the box contents before ordering.

faq.q: Do I need a Thunderbolt dock for a MacBook Pro?
faq.a: Not always. A USB-C hub like the Anker 8-in-1 works for basics. Choose Thunderbolt, such as the CalDigit TS4, for dual displays, fast drives or heavy charging.

faq.q: Can a dock give me more monitors than my Mac supports?
faq.a: Only with DisplayLink, which compresses video and needs drivers. Native Thunderbolt docks like the Plugable 16-in-1 stay within the chip's limit.

faq.q: Is the CalDigit TS4 worth it over the UGREEN Max 208?
faq.a: If you have many peripherals, yes: it has 18 ports against eight. For one monitor and a few devices, the UGREEN is enough.

faq.q: Will Thunderbolt 5 docks work on Thunderbolt 4 Macs?
faq.a: Yes, but they run at Thunderbolt 4 speed. The extra bandwidth is only used by a Thunderbolt 5 laptop.

faq.q: How much charging do I need?
faq.a: Around 85W to 100W suits most MacBook Pro models. Heavy 16 inch workloads may want more, as on the Anker Prime 14-Port at 160W.

faq.q: Do docks need drivers on a Mac?
faq.a: Thunderbolt docks like the Plugable models are driverless. DisplayLink based hubs need a driver for extra displays.

finalTake: For most MacBook Pro owners the CalDigit TS4 is the right dock: certified Thunderbolt 4, 18 ports and a Mac-first track record. The Plugable 16-in-1 is better if dual 4K monitors are your priority, and the UGREEN Revodok Max 208 saves money without leaving Thunderbolt. Reserve the TS5 Plus for Pro and Max owners with several displays, and use the Anker 8-in-1 only as a travel hub.
